pass_a_gloss: [...] of others, that Satan has been named a city, and this a strong one. For it is a custom for the God-inspired Scripture sometimes to liken the very most valiant to towers and walls or also cities, just as indeed we said earlier too, that the blessed prophet Jeremiah also has been set by God as a strong city and as a strong bronze wall. And Emmanuel having been shown forth and having shone upon the world, the unholy band of the opposing powers has been destroyed, and Satan was shaken from his very pits [another reading: foundations], and he has fallen thus, so as to fall into an endless weakness, and at no time to expect to rise up and lift his head again. [Lemma, Isaiah 25:3-5:] Because of this the poor people will bless you, and cities of men being wronged will bless you. For you became a helper to every lowly city, and to those who lost heart through want a shelter; from wicked men you will rescue them; a shelter of the thirsty, and breath of men being wronged. They will bless you as faint-souled men thirsting; in Zion, from ungodly men to whom you handed us over. Israel was called into knowledge of God through the tutoring in the Law, and was enriched with the things from God. For he was saved, and inherited the land of the promise. But the multitude of the other nations, being without measure, of those I mean throughout all under heaven, had been set wholly strangers to the spiritual and from-above goods, untasting of the gifts from God, naked in a certain way and unclothed, not holding up the divine shelter, not the covering from on high, not wealth into mind that from virtue, not any other of all the things that are full of praise and deemed worthy of all wonder. But since Christ himself appeared too, and taking them out of the greed of the devil he brought them to the God and Father, they have both been enriched with the light of the truth, the sharing of the glory from him, the greatness of the gospel way of life, and for these they send up the thank-offering songs to the God and Father. So since, he says, O Master, you also made an ancient and true counsel, summing up all things in Christ, and enlightening those in darkness, and pulling down the world-rulers of this age, although being as some cities so strong, the poor people will bless you, and whole cities will glorify you. For to all you became a helper, and a shelter to those unbearably grieved through poverty of the ancestral goods; and you rescued them from wicked men. For there were thus also in Zion some who had lost heart, just as indeed men who have thirsted. And perhaps through these things the prophet shows us that: for there were, there were in Israel too those thirsting for the Saviour's sojourn, and the Saviour of all [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … of others, that Satan has been called a city, and a strong one at that. For it is the custom of the God-inspired Scripture at times to liken the very mightiest to towers and walls, or even to cities. So, as we said earlier, even the blessed prophet Jeremiah was set by God as a fortified city and as a strong bronze wall (Jeremiah 1:18). But when Emmanuel was revealed and shone upon the world, the unholy throng of the opposing powers was destroyed, and Satan was shaken from his very foundations. He has fallen so as to sink into endless weakness, and he has no hope of ever rising again or lifting up his head.

“Therefore the poor people will bless you, and cities of men who are wronged will bless you. For you have become a helper to every lowly city, and a shelter to those who lost heart through want; you will rescue them from wicked men. A shelter for the thirsty, and the breath of men who are wronged. They will bless you as faint-hearted men who thirst in Zion, from ungodly men to whom you handed us over” (Isaiah 25:3–5).

Israel was called to the knowledge of God through the tutoring of the Law, and was made rich in the things that come from God; for it was saved, and inherited the land of the promise. But the countless multitude of the other nations, I mean those throughout the whole earth under heaven, had been utter strangers to the spiritual goods from above. They had no taste of the gifts that come from God. They were, in a way, naked and unclothed, having neither the divine shelter nor the covering from on high, neither the wealth of mind that comes from virtue nor anything else of all that is full of praise and counted worthy of every wonder. But when Christ himself appeared, he took them out of the devil’s grasping and brought them to God the Father. They have been made rich with the light of the truth, with a share in the glory that comes from him, and with the greatness of the gospel way of life; and for these things they send up songs of thanksgiving to God the Father.

So then, he says, O Master, since you have carried out an ancient and true counsel (Isaiah 25:1), summing up all things in Christ (Ephesians 1:10), enlightening those in darkness and casting down the world-rulers of this age (Ephesians 6:12), strong as cities though they were, the poor people will bless you, and whole cities will glorify you. For you have become a helper to every one of them, and a shelter to those unbearably grieved by their poverty in the goods of their fathers; and you rescued them from wicked men. For in Zion too there were some who had lost heart in this way, just like men who are thirsty. And perhaps by these words the prophet shows us this: there were, yes, there were in Israel too those who thirsted for the Savior’s coming, and the Savior of all …

choices.why: Jeremiah 1:18: it is Jeremiah whom God sets as a fortified city and bronze wall.
ἀναιρέω here of destruction, not lifting.
The edition's alternative βάθρων is followed; βαράθρων would give 'from the very pits'.

choices.english: the breath of men who are wronged
choices.why: Isaiah 25:4 Septuagint; ἀδικουμένων is passive: those who suffer wrong.
rejected: a spirit for men who do wrong

choices.why: Ephesians 6:12; the hostile powers Cyril had pictured as strong cities.
